To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neurons in the ferret auditory cortical field AI are sensitive to the spectrotemporal contrast of sounds, and that this sensitivity can be captured by contrast kernels that match up with STRFs.
(1) neurons in primary auditory cortex have contrast kernels, (2) contrast kernels are correlated with STRFs, and (3) contrast kernels are useful for modeling responses to natural sounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the statistics of the auditory environment are encoded in the responses of neurons in the primary auditory cortex.
the neural representation of auditory objects, and the neural representation of the statistical structure of the sounds that make up those objects.
the neural basis of auditory perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spectrotemporal receptive field and spectrotemporal contrast kernel of an auditory neuron are closely related.
the STRF and contrast kernel are two different but related measures of the same phenomenon.
our study provides the first demonstration that contrast kernels can be estimated from neural data, and that they are strongly correlated with the integration windows of the neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spectrotemporal kernels of neurons can be decomposed into two distinct components, one for the firing rate and one for the gain.
auditory cortex neurons are sensitive to both spectrotemporal features and their statistics.
neurons in primary auditory cortex integrate spectrotemporal features and contrast of the sound.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the spectrotemporal integration windows for cortical neurons are shaped not only by the sound statistics that they are sensitive to, but also the sound statistics that modulate their sensitivity to sound features.
auditory cortical neurons are not only selective for specific features of sounds, but they also respond differently when these features vary in their contrast.
auditory cortical neurons are sensitive to the statistics of sound, not just to its spectrotemporal structure.
